main_text.p: veniffe, atque in caufa fuiffe, ut hac dem haud amplius cogitârit: Rem autem ita ha- bere: Infantem cum fignum praberet, fe in terram demitti velle, vix in eapofitum ven- trem exonerâffe; nutricem autem illico batil- lum cineribus plenum arripuiffe, atque ex- crementa contegiffe, poftmodum vero omniam ignem projecisse. Hæc fuperftitiofa folli- citudo Illuftriss. Viri circa illum infan- tem occafionem præbuit Cacodæmo- ni, permittente Numine, luas fraudes fuamque operam mifcendi, dum objecta capacia, & ad fuperftitionem admitten- dam prona, Parentes offenderet: Quip pe non displicuit Nobili Viro (Parenti) nar- ratio Ill. Comitis; ipfaque mater fe ex- cufabat, quod in corrigenda circa infantem mala illa confuetudine major non fuerit ad- hibita diligentia, &c. Certè meis infan- tibus, quos majori fiduciâ Deo commendo, quàm ut metuam impostoris e rebus ludicris fraudes, veleffectum ex fuperftitione, qui in rerum natura rationem non inveniat, nil tale ex fimili caufa

page.notes: The page is printed with heavy show-through and damaged right-edge lines; the text is reconstructed from the scan where letters were uncertain. The final words in the right margin appear to be a catchword "caufa". Some words near line ends (e.g. "Cacodæmoni", "fimili") are doubtful.
